notes: Both LLM and peer reviewers agree that claims about virus 'perception' and appropriation of host sensory systems (C8, C102, C104, C126) are insufficiently supported. Peer reviewers explicitly request rephrasing title/abstract, stating the hypothesis is plausible but not adequately investigated. LLM similarly notes these claims are interpretive and speculative, requiring additional mechanistic studies.

Strong agreement on P2-TC mutant experiments (C86-C96). Both recognize these genetic experiments as core contributions demonstrating TB transformation's role in transmission. Peer reviewers affirm the findings as 'original and significant contributions' with no concerns raised about the mutant data.

Disagreement on interpretive synthesis claims (C103, C105, C106). LLM finds the distinction between TB transformation and plant defense responses well-supported by timing and mechanistic data. Peer reviewers question whether the evidence justifies strong statements about virus appropriation of host machinery, suggesting these interpretive claims exceed the data.

Complete agreement on TB morphotype identification (C35-C43). Both recognize the immunofluorescence microscopy data clearly establishing three distinct TB types. Peer reviewers accept these core experimental observations as original contributions, with requests for additional images being for presentation enhancement, not due to doubts about findings.

Agreement on aphid feeding triggering TB transformation (C69-C74). Both accept the statistical evidence (p<0.0001) and reversibility data. Peer reviewers include these claims in their affirmation of 'original and significant contributions' regarding stress-triggered TB reorganization.

Agreement on central finding that TB transformation is required for efficient transmission (C3-C7). Both recognize converging evidence from pharmacological and genetic approaches. Peer reviewers explicitly affirm that mixed networks mediate viral transmission as an original contribution.

Agreement on electron microscopy findings showing differential effects of stresses on TB ultrastructure (C63-C67). Peer reviewers accept these observations as part of the core experimental findings on TB transformation and component redistribution.

Agreement on azide-induced mixed-networks enhancing transmission (C75-C77). Both accept the statistical evidence (p<0.0001) and critical controls. Peer reviewers implicitly accept these pharmacological experiments as part of the affirmed contributions on transmission mediation.

Agreement on virus particle redistribution onto microtubules in mixed-networks (C58-C61). Both accept the convergent evidence from immunofluorescence, TEM, and immunogold labeling. Peer reviewers include this in their acceptance of TB reorganization findings.

Agreement on heat shock not enhancing transmission (C78, C83). Both recognize this negative result as important for establishing that mixed-network formation, not just tubulin accumulation, is required. Peer reviewers accept the transmission assay data without concerns.

Agreement on differential effects of stresses on TB transformation (C44-C46). Both accept the systematic immunofluorescence experiments showing stress-specific responses. Peer reviewers affirm these observations as part of the core discovery.

Agreement on temporal sequence and reversibility of TB transformation (C55-C57). Both accept the time-course experiments and quantitative kinetics data. Peer reviewers include these findings in their affirmation of the TB reorganization discovery.

Agreement on rapid kinetics of TB transformation (C48-C49). Both accept the ~10 second timescale demonstrated through wounding and microelectrode experiments. Peer reviewers include this in their acceptance of the stress-triggered reorganization findings.

Agreement on CO2-induced mixed-networks enhancing plant-to-plant transmission (C79). Both accept the statistical evidence (p=0.0025). Peer reviewers implicitly accept this as part of the transmission mediation findings they affirm.

Partial disagreement on accessibility hypothesis (C84). LLM finds the hypothesis logical but mechanistically unproven, wanting direct evidence of increased virus acquisition. Peer reviewers appear to accept this as part of the transmission mediation mechanism they affirm, though they don't explicitly address the mechanistic details.

Agreement on oryzalin preventing mixed-network formation (C85). Both accept this pharmacological evidence supporting the role of intact microtubules. Peer reviewers implicitly accept this as part of the affirmed transmission findings.

FRAP experiments on tubulin dynamics (C51-C52) only explicitly evaluated by LLM. Peer reviewers don't specifically comment on these claims, though they accept the overall TB transformation findings. No evidence of disagreement, but no explicit peer review assessment of these specific experiments.

Uncertainty about virus particle origin in mixed-networks (C98) only explicitly addressed by LLM. Peer reviewers don't comment on this specific mechanistic question. LLM notes authors acknowledge this uncertainty.
